source_text:
Ἀναπέμψαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὸ ἀμὴν καὶ πληρώσαντος τὴν εὐχήν, οἱ τοῦ πυρὸς ἄνθρωποι ἐξῆψαν τὸ πῦρ. μεγάλης δὲ ἐκλαμψάσης φλογός, θαῦμα εἴδομεν, οἷς ἰδεῖν ἐδόθη: οἳ καὶ ἐτηρήθημεν εἰς τὸ ἀναγγεῖλαι τοῖς λοιποῖς τὰ γενόμενα.
τὸ γὰρ πῦρ καμάρας εἶδος ποιῆσαν, ὥσπερ ὀθόνη πλοίου ὑπὸ πνεύματος πληρουμένη, κύκλῳ περιετείχισεν τὸ σῶμα τοῦ μάρτυρος: καὶ ἦν μέσον οὐχ ὡς σὰρξ καιομένη, ἀλλ’ ὡς ἄρτος ὀπτώμενος ἢ ὡς χρυσὸς καὶ ἄργυρος ἐν καμίνῳ πυρούμενος. καὶ γὰρ εὐωδίας τοσαύτης ἀντελαβόμεθα, ὡς λιβανωτοῦ πνέοντος ἢ ἄλλου τινὸς τῶν τιμίων ἀρωμάτων.
orientation: Polycarp has just finished his prayer before the pyre, and the men in charge of the fire now light it.
pass_a_gloss: And when he had sent up the amen and completed the prayer, the men of the fire kindled the fire. And when a great flame blazed out, we saw a wonder, to whom it was given to see; who also were kept safe for the purpose of reporting to the rest the things that happened. For the fire, having made the shape of a vaulted chamber, just as a ship's sail being filled by wind, walled around in a circle the body of the martyr; and he was in the middle not as burning flesh, but as bread being baked or as gold and silver being refined in a furnace. For we also perceived so great a fragrance, as of frankincense breathing or of some other of the precious spices.

choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the source's periphrastic expression for those in charge of the pyre.
Keeps the noun 'wonder' as the object, matching the source's emphasis on the miraculous sight.

choices.english: having made the shape of a vaulted chamber
choices.why: Literal rendering of the architectural image, preserving the visual comparison.
rejected: having taken the form of a dome

choices.why: Literal rendering of the baking image, which contrasts with burning flesh.
rejected: as a loaf in the oven

choices.why: Preserves the personified verb 'breathing' for the fragrance, matching the source's vivid metaphor.

pass_b_english: When Polycarp had sent up his Amen and completed the prayer, the men in charge of the fire kindled it. A great flame blazed out, and we saw a wonder. We were the ones permitted to see it, and we were kept safe so that we could report to the rest what happened.

The fire took the shape of a vaulted chamber, like a ship's sail filled with wind, and it stood around the martyr's body like a wall. He was in the middle, not like burning flesh, but like bread being baked, or like gold and silver being refined in a furnace. We also perceived such a rich fragrance, as if frankincense were breathing or some other precious spice.

polish.changed: Clarified that Polycarp is the one who prayed, identified the witnesses explicitly, and smoothed the sentence flow while preserving every detail.

Clarified the first-person plural as the eyewitnesses from the church in Smyrna, smoothed the fire imagery by replacing 'walled around' with 'stood around like a wall,' and made the sentence rhythm more natural for reading aloud.

notes.why: The imagery is confusing and the verb “walled” is misused.
notes.fix: Rephrase: “The flames rose like a vaulted canopy, surrounding his body without consuming it.”

edits.new: The fire took the shape of a vaulted chamber, like a ship's sail filled with wind, and it encircled the martyr's body.

fixed: The first problem was real: 'walled' was misused; changed to 'encircled' to match the source's 'walled around in a circle' while keeping the imagery clear.
